In GSI, this manifests as a signal-to-noise problem where coach commands corrupt the tactical signal. The quarterback's cognitive load becomes a bottleneck when trying to process both field dynamics and sideline instructions. This leads to a degradation in decision quality. In GSE, the system must model the interaction between autonomous agents and external influence. The failure mode occurs when the coach's input exceeds the agent's capacity to integrate it without error. The mathematical structure reveals a trade-off between information fidelity and control authority. Asymptotically, teams that rely on autonomous decision-making outperform those under centralized direction because they avoid the information bottleneck inherent in side-line communication. The epistemic trace shows that this principle applies across domains—sports, robotics, and organizational design—where decentralized cognition prevails over top-down orchestration.
